The unique optimizer obeys a first-order equation whose derivative at w=E is sign(p-pcrit). The T-derivative of truncated-exponential mean is positive, proving the strict direction law. Uniform short/long horizon convergence and exponential charging/retention complete the claim. Standalone code passed 6636 bounded checks across 108 parameter families; these are supporting evidence, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact constant-load fixed-duration discharge optimization resolves a natural operational gap between already established instantaneous maximum power and quasistatic time-dependent load protocols. It gives all-parameter uniqueness, a new sharp state-of-charge threshold for opposite horizon responses, and exact charge/aging times when the direction changes. This structural phase boundary is motivated by a physical design constraint, not an arbitrary finite parameter choice or small numerical gain. Its applicability is restricted to ideal two-state Markov kinetics.
